title: 3.3.22 Lab: Read and Update a Nested Array
description: Read and reassign values in a nested array with double-index syntax, then sum every cell with a nested loop. Auto-graded: the code runs and the final grid and total are checked.

steps.title: Start with the grid
steps.instructions: The starter already creates the grid: let grid = [[1, 2], [3, 4]];. Leave that line exactly as it is.

steps.title: Log one inner value
steps.instructions: Use double-index syntax, grid[1][0], to console.log the value in row 1, column 0. It prints 3.

steps.title: Update one inner value
steps.instructions: Reassign that same cell with grid[1][0] = 8.

steps.title: Sum every number
steps.instructions: Create a variable called total. Use a nested loop (outer over rows, inner over cells) to add up every number in the grid, then console.log the total.

requirements.title: nested array literal present
requirements.description: Code declares a nested array. Help: 3.3.20 (Lists Inside Lists)
requirements.hint: The grid is a list of lists, written like [[1, 2], [3, 4]]. The starter already has it.

requirements.title: double-index access present
requirements.description: Code reads or writes with two indexes. Help: 3.3.20 (Lists Inside Lists)
requirements.hint: Read a cell with two indexes: grid[row][column], for example grid[1][0].

requirements.title: nested for loops present
requirements.description: A for loop sits inside another for loop (braces optional). Help: 3.3.20 (Lists Inside Lists)
requirements.hint: Put one for loop inside another: the outer one visits the rows, the inner one visits the cells of a row.

requirements.title: console.log present
requirements.description: Code calls console.log. Help: 3.3.20 (Lists Inside Lists)
requirements.hint: Print with console.log: the cell's old value first, then the total at the end.

requirements.title: a grid cell is updated
requirements.description: Code changes one cell with a double index and an assignment, like grid[1][0] = 8 (writing a cell back to itself changes nothing). Help: 3.3.20 (Lists Inside Lists)
requirements.hint: Write a new value into one cell with two indexes, like grid[1][0] = 8. Writing a cell back to itself changes nothing.

requirements.title: a running total is logged
requirements.description: Code adds numbers into a total with += (or total = total + ...) and then logs that total. Help: 3.3.20 (Lists Inside Lists)
requirements.hint: Start total at 0, add each cell to it inside the inner loop (total += ...), then console.log(total) after the loops.

requirements.title: grid ends updated and total adds every cell
requirements.description: After the code runs, grid is [[1, 2], [8, 4]] (only the cell grid[1][0] changed) and total equals the sum of every cell of the updated grid. Help: 3.3.20 (Lists Inside Lists)

checks.fail: total should be the sum of every cell in grid AFTER the update. Add up the grid once the cell has been changed.

requirements.hint: Change grid[1][0] to 8 BEFORE you add things up. Then total adds 1 + 2 + 8 + 4. Check the loop visits every row and every cell.

requirements.title: the old cell value and the total are printed
requirements.description: The output shows 3 (the cell's value before the update) and 15 (the total of the updated grid). Help: 3.3.20 (Lists Inside Lists)
requirements.hint: Print grid[1][0] before you change it (3), and print total after the loops (15).
